summary: Diablo franchise entries added as supplemental sourced guide rows; Sami did not list these in the locked personal spine.

entries.title: Diablo
entries.definitive_edition: Diablo + Hellfire on GOG for Windows

primary.why: Diablo released on Windows, PlayStation, and Mac OS, with the Hellfire expansion later included as a free add-on with the GOG release. The Windows GOG release is the best archive route because it preserves the base game plus the expansion option on a modern PC path.
primary.how_to_play: Use Diablo + Hellfire on GOG for Windows. Play the base game first, then Hellfire as optional expansion content because it was not originally a Blizzard-labeled product.

entries.remaster_caveats: Hellfire is included with the GOG purchase but should be labeled as optional expansion content, not part of the original base-game run.

entries.title: Diablo II

primary.why: Diablo II released on Windows and Mac, then Diablo II: Resurrected brought the game to Windows, PlayStation, Xbox, and Switch. Windows Resurrected is the best archive route because it includes the remastered presentation, Lord of Destruction content, current official updates, and the highest capture/settings ceiling.
primary.how_to_play: Use Diablo II: Resurrected on Windows through Battle.net or Steam, with the current expansion/update state documented. Keep the classic Windows/Mac releases for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Resurrected has online/account requirements that differ from the classic releases; preserve classic PC separately for historical behavior.

entries.title: Diablo III
entries.definitive_edition: Current Windows release with Reaper of Souls and Rise of the Necromancer

primary.version: Current PC release with Reaper of Souls and Rise of the Necromancer
primary.why: Diablo III released on Windows and macOS, then PlayStation and Xbox consoles, and later Switch as Eternal Collection. Windows is the best archive route because it has the highest display/capture ceiling and full expansion/class content through the PC ecosystem.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows release with Reaper of Souls and Rise of the Necromancer content installed. Use console versions only for local-co-op or platform comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Console versions have different control/local-play behavior; use them for comparison only.

entries.title: Diablo Immortal

primary.why: Diablo Immortal released on Android and iOS with a Windows beta/client route. Windows is the best archive route because it has the strongest capture/display path for the live-service MMO ARPG, while mobile remains the design-origin route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows client and document service/version state before capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live-service state and monetization/content availability should be documented at capture time.

entries.title: Diablo IV
entries.definitive_edition: Current Windows release with Vessel of Hatred and Lord of Hatred

primary.version: Current PC release with Vessel of Hatred and Lord of Hatred
primary.why: Diablo IV released on PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S, with Vessel of Hatred and Lord of Hatred expansions extending the current content set. Windows is the best archive route because it has the highest display/settings/capture ceiling for the live-service current build.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows release with the latest expansion content installed. Document season, patch, and expansion ownership at capture time.

entries.remaster_caveats: Seasonal/live-service content changes over time; archive the exact patch and expansion state.
